record.original_question: Let Pi(n) be the product of the decimal digits of n and let Pm(n) be the first iterate count at which repeated application of Pi stabilizes. Is it true that every natural number n has multiplicative persistence at most 11, that is, Pm(n) <= 11?

evidence.quote: Problem 31 (Conjecture of multiplicative persistence). Given n in N, let Pi(n) be the product of all its digits. Set Pm(n) ... Is it true that for all n in N, Pm(n) <= 11?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$ written in base $10$, let $\Pi(n)$ denote the product of the decimal digits of $n$. Define a sequence by $n_0 = n$ and $n_{k+1} = \Pi(n_k)$. Since $\Pi(n) < n$ whenever $n \geq 10$, this sequence eventually reaches a single-digit number; let $P_m(n)$ denote the smallest nonnegative integer $k$ such that $n_k$ has only one decimal digit (equivalently, $n_k < 10$). The quantity $P_m(n)$ is called the multiplicative persistence of $n$.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $n$, $P_m(n) \leq 11$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is Sloane's multiplicative persistence conjecture (1973). The smallest known number with persistence 11 is 277777788888899, and no number with persistence ≥ 12 has been found despite extensive computer searches (up to roughly 10^{300} and beyond). The conjecture remains open; only partial results exist (e.g., bounds restricting where larger-persistence numbers could occur).

status_evidence.title: Persistence of a number - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The smallest numbers with multiplicative persistence 0,1,...,11 are known; no number below 10^{233} (and per further searches, much higher) has persistence greater than 11. It is conjectured that 11 is the maximum.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that multiplicative persistence is bounded by 11 is widely cited as open.

status_evidence.title: OEIS A003001
status_evidence.snippet: Smallest number of multiplicative persistence n. Sequence ends at 277777788888899 (persistence 11); no further terms are known.
status_evidence.claim: No number with persistence > 11 has been found; conjecture remains unresolved.
